rows.title: Support redirecting `--help` to a man page
rows.body:
### Context

We have a rather complicated `--help` documentation which would like to forward it to sphinx for the generation. We would still like to have the complete help shown initially, and the closest thing would be to redirect it to a `man ...` call similar to how `git ... --help` does.

### Current state

It can be hacked around to support this by manually handling the `--help`, but a first-party integration would be more appreciated. Probably also a plugin could be made to support in the meantime.

Edit: although that is not very straightforward 🙃

### Design suggestion

On the user side this should support:
- redirecting `--help` to a `man` page (or any other redirect)
- check a environment variable to decide if the long help or short help should be shown/trigerred
- `get_help` etc. should continue to give the short help version

rows.title: [rejected AI] click.Path.to_info_dict() and PathInfoDict omit resolve_path and executable
rows.body:
`click.Path.to_info_dict()` and its typing definition `PathInfoDict` in `src/click/types.py` do not serialize the `resolve_path` and `executable` attributes.

While the other boolean parameters (`exists`, `file_okay`, `dir_okay`, `writable`, `readable`, `allow_dash`) are included, `resolve_path` and `executable` are missing from both `Path.to_info_dict()` and `PathInfoDict`.

### Reproduction

```python
import click

p = click.Path(executable=True, resolve_path=True)
info = p.to_info_dict()

# Missing keys in output:
assert "executable" in info, "executable missing from to_info_dict"
assert "resolve_path" in info, "resolve_path missing from to_info_dict"
```

### Actual Behavior

```python
{
    'exists': False, 
    'file_okay': True, 
    'dir_okay': True, 
    'writable': False, 
    'readable': True, 
    'allow_dash': False, 
    'param_type': 'Path', 
    'name': 'path'
}
```

### Expected Behavior

`info` should include `'resolve_path': True` and `'executable': True` (and default to `False`), and `PathInfoDict` should declare `resolve_path: bool` and `executable: bool`.

### Environment

- Python version: 3.13 (reproducible on all versions)
- Click version: `main` / `8.1.8`

---

I have a patch with regression test coverage in `tests/test_info_dict.py` verified against the test suite and would be happy to submit a PR if this is welcome.

rows.title: [rejected AI] Case-insensitive Choice completion misses Unicode case-folding matches
rows.body:
### Description

`Choice` uses `casefold()` for case-insensitive conversion, but `shell_complete()` lowercases the incomplete value and compares it with `lower()`. This makes completion fail for Unicode case-folding expansions.

For example, `Choice(["ẞ"], case_sensitive=False)` accepts `"ß"` during conversion because both values case-fold to `"ss"`, but completion for the incomplete value `"ß"` returns no suggestion because `"ss".lower().startswith("ß")` is false.

### Steps to reproduce

```python
from click import Choice

choice = Choice(["ẞ"], case_sensitive=False)
assert choice.convert("ß", None, None) == "ẞ"

# A completion callback using this Choice receives incomplete="ß".
# It currently produces no completion item, even though the normalized choice is "ss".
```

The relevant implementation is `Choice.shell_complete()` in `src/click/types.py`; it uses `lower()` while `normalize_choice()` uses `casefold()`.

### Expected behavior

Case-insensitive shell completion should use the same Unicode-aware normalization as conversion and return the normalized `"ss"` suggestion for incomplete `"ß"`.

### Actual behavior

No completion item is returned.

### Environment

- Latest `main` at the time of filing
- Python 3.12+
- Click shell completion

I searched existing issues and pull requests for Unicode casefolding and Choice completion and did not find a matching report. A regression test covering `ẞ`/`ß` would prevent this from recurring.

rows.title: [rejected AI] `BOOL` raises `AttributeError` on numeric input since 8.2.2
rows.body:
`BOOL` crashes with `AttributeError` when it receives a number instead of a
string. Command line values are always strings, so this only shows up when a
number reaches the converter from inside the program: a boolean option with
`default=1` or `default=0`, a `default_map` loaded from a config file where a
boolean came through as a number, or `click.prompt(type=bool)` with a numeric
default. `--help` still works, so the failure only appears at invocation.

Click 8.0 through 8.2.1 accepted `0` and `1` through the `value in {False, True}`
guard added in e79c2b4. #2956 (released in 8.2.2) replaced it with
`isinstance(value, bool)` while reworking `str_to_bool`, so numbers now fall
through to `value.strip()`. 

Minimal reproduction:

```python
import click
click.BOOL(1)
```

As a command:

```python
import click


@click.command()
@click.option("--verbose", is_flag=True, default=1)
def cli(verbose):
    click.echo(f"verbose={verbose}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    cli()
```

```text
$ python cli.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../click/core.py", line 2565, in type_cast_value
    return convert(value)
  File ".../click/core.py", line 2540, in convert
    return self.type(value, param=self, ctx=ctx)
  File ".../click/types.py", line 90, in __call__
    return self.convert(value, param, ctx)
  File ".../click/types.py", line 860, in convert
    normalized = self.str_to_bool(value)
  File ".../click/types.py", line 857, in str_to_bool
    return BoolParamType.bool_states.get(value.strip().lower())
                                         ^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'strip'
```

Expected: `click.BOOL(1)` returns `True` and `click.BOOL(0)` returns `False`,
as in 8.0 through 8.2.1, and the command above prints `verbose=True`. Any
other non-string value should produce the normal
`... is not a valid boolean` usage error rather than a traceback.

Environment:

- Python version: 3.12.13
- Click version: 8.5.0 and `main` (36baa15); every release since 8.2.2

rows.title: [rejected AI] Envvar for multiple=True + nargs>1 silently drops incomplete trailing tokens
rows.body:
﻿When an option uses `multiple=True` and `nargs > 1`, an environment-variable value whose whitespace-split token count is **not a multiple of `nargs`** is accepted with exit code 0, and the trailing incomplete group is **silently discarded**.

The same values on the CLI are rejected (e.g. `Got unexpected extra argument`). Non-multiple `nargs > 1` options already reject incomplete envvar values with `BadParameter` (`Takes N values but M were given.`). The `multiple=True` path should do the same instead of truncating.

Root cause: `Option.value_from_envvar()` calls `batch()`, which uses `zip(..., strict=False)` and drops remainder tokens.

## Reproduction

```python
import click
from click.testing import CliRunner

runner = CliRunner()

@click.command()
@click.option("--arg", nargs=2, multiple=True)
def cli(arg):
    click.echo(repr(arg))

# Envvar: silently drops "c"
r = runner.invoke(cli, [], auto_envvar_prefix="TEST", env={"TEST_ARG": "a b c"})
print(r.exit_code, r.output.strip())
# Actual: 0  "(('a', 'b'),)"

# CLI: rejects the extra token
r2 = runner.invoke(cli, ["--arg", "a", "b", "c"])
print(r2.exit_code)
print(r2.output)
# Actual: exit 2, "Got unexpected extra argument (c)"
```

Also reproduces with `envvar="ARG"` and `env={"ARG": "a b c"}`.

With five tokens (`"a b c d e"`), the result is `(('a', 'b'), ('c', 'd'))` — `e` is silently discarded.

## Expected behavior

Envvar parsing should raise `BadParameter` (same family of arity error used for non-multiple `nargs` envvars), instead of silently dropping tokens and exiting 0.

## Environment

- Python version: 3.12.10
- Click version: main @ 36baa15 (8.5.1 unreleased)

**AI assistance disclosure:** This bug report was prepared with assistance from Cursor (AI coding agent). I reproduced and validated the behavior locally.

rows.title: [rejected AI] count=True ignores non-zero default when counting flags
rows.body:
<!--
This issue tracker is a tool to address bugs in Click itself. Please use
GitHub Discussions or the Pallets Discord for questions about your own code.

Replace this comment with a clear outline of what the bug is.
-->

When an option uses `count=True` with a non-zero `default`, each occurrence of the flag counts from **0** instead of from the configured default. Passing fewer flags than the default can therefore produce a value **lower than the default** (or leave `default=1` unchanged when the flag is passed once).

This differs from `argparse.ArgumentParser` with `action="count"`, which increments relative to the default (for example `default=3` plus one flag occurrence yields `4`).

<!--
Describe how to replicate the bug.

Include a minimal reproducible example that demonstrates the bug.
Include the full traceback if there was an exception.
-->

```python
import argparse
import click
from click.testing import CliRunner

# argparse (expected-aligned behavior)
p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument("-v", action="count", default=3)
print("argparse no flags", p.parse_args([]).v)        # 3
print("argparse one flag", p.parse_args(["-v"]).v)    # 4
print("argparse two flags", p.parse_args(["-vv"]).v)  # 5

# click
@click.command()
@click.option("-v", count=True, default=3)
def cli(v):
    click.echo(v)

runner = CliRunner()
print("click no flags", runner.invoke(cli, []).output.strip())       # 3
print("click one flag", runner.invoke(cli, ["-v"]).output.strip())   # 1  ← bug
print("click two flags", runner.invoke(cli, ["-vv"]).output.strip()) # 2  ← bug
```

Root cause appears to be in `click/parser.py`, where the count action always starts from `0`:

```python
state.opts[self.dest] = state.opts.get(self.dest, 0) + 1
```

Once a command-line count is present, `consume_value()` takes that value and never applies the option default as a baseline.

<!--
Describe the expected behavior that should have happened but didn't.
-->

Expected (argparse-compatible): command-line counts are **additive** on top of the option default.

| Invocation | Expected | Actual (Click) |
|---|---|---|
| `(none)` | `3` | `3` |
| one `-v` | `4` | `1` |
| `-vv` | `5` | `2` |
| `-vvv` | `6` | `3` |

With `default=1`, a single flag occurrence should yield `2`, but currently yields `1` (same as omitting the flag).

Environment:

- Python version: 3.12.10
- Click version: 8.5.1.dev0 (main)

rows.title: [rejected AI] Literal mutable default silently accumulates mutations across CliRunner.invoke() calls with a pass-through ParamType
rows.body:
**AI disclosure:** this was investigated and written with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic). I independently reproduced it against a fresh clone of `main` myself before filing.

## Summary

A literal mutable default (e.g. `default=[]`, `default={}`) on an `Option` silently accumulates mutations across separate command invocations within one process, when combined with a `ParamType` whose `convert()` validates and returns the value unchanged (e.g. `type=click.UNPROCESSED`, or any custom type handling structured data like a JSON/dict param).

This is the classic Python mutable-default-argument trap — Click's own docs correctly recommend `default=list`/`default=dict` (a callable factory) as the safe pattern, and that path genuinely works. But a literal mutable default only gets protected from this trap by accident, when the default type-coercion path happens to stringify/rebuild the value (e.g. plain `--items` with no `type=` routes through `StringParamType`). Nothing actually copies the default before handing it to the callback.

## Reproduction

```python
import click
from click.testing import CliRunner

@click.command()
@click.option("--items", type=click.UNPROCESSED, default=[])
def cmd(items):
    items.append("x")
    click.echo(f"len={len(items)}")

runner = CliRunner()
print(runner.invoke(cmd, []).output.strip())  # len=1
print(runner.invoke(cmd, []).output.strip())  # len=2  <- same list object, not reset
print(runner.invoke(cmd, []).output.strip())  # len=3
```

Confirmed against current `main`: `id(items)` is identical across all three calls.

## Root cause

`Parameter.get_default()` (`click/core.py:2445-2476`) only special-cases *callable* defaults (`if call and callable(value): value = value()`, line 2473) — a literal default value is returned as-is, no copy. `type_cast_value`/`consume_value` never copy it either before it reaches the callback.

The reason a plain `default=[]` doesn't normally show this (and why it's easy to miss): Click's type-inference (`click/types.py` `_guess_type`) routes an untyped list default through `StringParamType`, which effectively rebuilds the value rather than passing the same object through. `type=click.UNPROCESSED` (documented, and the natural choice for custom structured-data types) explicitly opts out of that coercion — and loses the incidental protection along with it.

## Scope

Only manifests in a long-running process that invokes the same command repeatedly — a test suite using `CliRunner.invoke()` in a loop, a REPL-style tool, or any host process embedding Click commands. A single-shot CLI invocation never notices, since the process exits after one call.

Checked `gh search issues --repo pallets/click` for "mutable default", "default list shared", "get_default copy" — no matching prior report found.

Happy to put together a PR (something like: deep-copy a literal mutable default via `copy.deepcopy` in `get_default()`, mirroring the protection callable defaults already get) if this is confirmed worth fixing.

rows.title: Terminal escape-sequence injection in error messages
rows.body:
### Summary
Click is vulnerable to terminal escape-sequence injection because command-line tokens are interpolated raw into error messages that are written to the user's terminal without control-character filtering.

Verified on Click at commit https://github.com/pallets/click/commit/36baa15ff831b939a22bc527cd76ce653ef6f66d (8.5.1.dev0).
### Details
Click reflects unsanitised `argv` tokens into error output at two locations:

`click/src/click/core.py:1391` interpolates the raw tokens:

```python
ngettext(
    "Got unexpected extra argument ({args})",
    "Got unexpected extra arguments ({args})",
    len(args),
).format(args=" ".join(map(str, args)))
```

`click/src/click/types.py:1013` interpolates the raw filename:

```python
self.fail(
    f"'{format_filename(value)}': {e.strerror}",
    param,
    ctx,
)
```

Both reach the terminal through `echo()` (`utils.py:324`), whose only sanitisation is `strip_ansi()`. That sanitisation does not apply here, for two independent reasons:

- `should_strip_ansi()` (`_compat.py:499-506`) returns `not isatty(stream)`, so stripping is skipped entirely when the stream is a terminal.
- `_ansi_re` (`_compat.py:19`) is `r"\033\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]"`, which matches only 7-bit CSI. OSC, DCS, APC, 8-bit C1 (`\x9b`), `ESC c`, and bare C0 controls (`\r`, `\b`) are never stripped.

Consequently an attacker-supplied token is delivered to the terminal emulator byte-for-byte. This permits window-title spoofing (OSC 0), forged program output by moving the cursor and overwriting earlier lines (CSI / `\r`), attacker-controlled hyperlinks under arbitrary anchor text (OSC 8), and — on terminals where clipboard write is enabled — silently staging a shell command in the victim's clipboard for their next paste (OSC 52).

### PoC
1. Create a file named `poc.py` with the following content:
```python
import click
 
@click.command()
@click.option("--f", type=click.File("r"))
def cli(f):
    click.echo("ok")
 
if __name__ == "__main__":
    cli()
```
2. Run the Python script:
```
python3 poc.py $(echo -en '\x0dOVERWRITTEN USING ESCAPE SEQUENCE')
```
3. Observe that the raw escape bytes reach the terminal.

### Suggested Remediation
Apply `!r` at both reflection sites, matching the convention already used everywhere else in the codebase:

```diff
diff --git a/src/click/core.py b/src/click/core.py
index de129ec..5c6c9de 100644
--- a/src/click/core.py
+++ b/src/click/core.py
@@ -1391,7 +1391,7 @@ class Command:
                     "Got unexpected extra argument ({args})",
                     "Got unexpected extra arguments ({args})",
                     len(args),
-                ).format(args=" ".join(map(str, args)))
+                ).format(args=" ".join(map(repr, args)))
             )
 
         ctx.args = args
diff --git a/src/click/types.py b/src/click/types.py
index 0eb8462..2d9e30f 100644
--- a/src/click/types.py
+++ b/src/click/types.py
@@ -1010,7 +1010,7 @@ class File(ParamType[t.IO[t.Any]]):
             return f
         except OSError as e:
             self.fail(
-                f"'{format_filename(value)}': {e.strerror}",
+                f"'{format_filename(value)!r}': {e.strerror}",
                 param,
                 ctx,
             )
diff --git a/tests/test_arguments.py b/tests/test_arguments.py
index fea48cc..5a0e3e3 100644
--- a/tests/test_arguments.py
+++ b/tests/test_arguments.py
@@ -76,7 +76,7 @@ def test_nargs_err(runner):
 
     result = runner.invoke(copy, ["foo", "bar"])
     assert result.exit_code == 2
-    assert "Got unexpected extra argument (bar)" in result.output
+    assert "Got unexpected extra argument ('bar')" in result.output
 
 
 def test_bytes_args(runner, monkeypatch):
```

### Credits
Found by [OSTIF](https://ostif.org/) using AI with their own harness.
Manually verified, fixed, and reported by [Shielder](https://www.shielder.com/).

rows.title: Nightly "Stress" jobs run the normal test suite; the stress tests never execute
rows.body:
The four `test_stress_*` tests do not run in CI, or anywhere else. The nightly Stress jobs run the ordinary test suite with those tests deselected.

### Why

`pyproject.toml:91` deselects them globally:

```toml
addopts = "-m 'not stress'"
```

`pyproject.toml:178-183` defines an environment that overrides it, and that environment is correct:

```toml
[tool.tox.env.stress]
commands = [["pytest", "-v", "--tb=short", "-x", "-m", "stress",
             "--basetemp={env_tmp_dir}", "--override-ini=addopts=", ...]]
```

But `nightly.yaml:27-29` does not run `stress`. It runs `stress-py3.14` and `stress-py3.14t`, which are listed in `env_list` at `pyproject.toml:150`:

```yaml
- {name: Stress 3.14,     python: '3.14',  tox: stress-py3.14}
- {name: Stress 3.14t,    python: '3.14t', tox: stress-py3.14t}
- {name: Stress Mac 3.14t, python: '3.14t', tox: stress-py3.14t, os: macos-latest}
```

tox's TOML source does not decompose factors for `[tool.tox.env.<name>]`, so `stress-py3.14` does not inherit from `[tool.tox.env.stress]`. It is generated from `env_run_base` instead.

### Reproducing

With tox 4.52.0 (the version in `uv.lock:1370`) and tox-uv:

```
$ tox config -e stress-py3.14
commands = pytest -v --tb=short --basetemp=<workdir>/stress-py3.14/tmp
base     = tool.tox.env_run_base

$ tox config -e stress
commands = pytest -v --tb=short -x -m stress --basetemp=<workdir>/stress/tmp --override-ini=addopts=
```

`stress-py3.14` gets neither `-m stress` nor `--override-ini=addopts=`, so it inherits `-m 'not stress'` and runs the normal suite. The `py3.14` factor *is* honoured (`base_python = py3.14`), which is what makes the name look like it worked; the `stress-` prefix matches nothing.

No warning is emitted — stderr is empty, and `tox -vv config -e stress-py3.14` produces no mention of an unmatched name. `tox config -e totally-made-up-env` does fail with "provided environments not found in configuration file", so the name resolves specifically because `env_list` contains it.

### Not running anywhere

- `tests/test_stream_lifecycle.py:495` `test_stress_thread_pool_with_exit`

rows.title: [rejected AI] Atomic `open_file`: path-based `chmod` can follow a symlink, and a failed `chmod` leaks the fd
rows.body:
`click.open_file(..., atomic=True)` (and `click.File` with `atomic=True`) creates a sibling temp file with `os.open(..., O_CREAT|O_EXCL)`, then:

```python
fd = os.open(tmp_filename, flags, 0o666 if perm is None else perm)
if perm is not None:
    os.chmod(tmp_filename, perm)  # restore bits umask stripped
```

The atomic branch has two related problems:

1. **Leaked fd.** If `os.chmod` raises, `fd` is never closed and never wrapped in a file object. The exception propagates from `open_stream`.
2. **chmod by name.** `os.open` already has `fd`. Linux `os.chmod(path)` follows symlinks. Between `open` and `chmod`, a writer who can create names in the destination directory can replace `tmp_filename` with a symlink; `chmod` then changes the **target** of that symlink. `os.fchmod(fd, perm)` would only touch the inode that was just created.

# Reproduction


## 1) Leaked fd when `chmod` fails

```python
import errno
import os
import tempfile

import click

workdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
dest = os.path.join(workdir, "target.txt")
with open(dest, "w") as f:
    f.write("old\n")
os.chmod(dest, 0o644)

real_chmod = os.chmod

def boom_chmod(path, mode, *args, **kwargs):
    if os.path.basename(str(path)).startswith(".__atomic-write"):
        raise OSError(errno.EPERM, "chmod denied", path)
    return real_chmod(path, mode, *args, **kwargs)

before = len(os.listdir("/proc/self/fd"))
os.chmod = boom_chmod
try:
    click.open_file(dest, "w", atomic=True)
except OSError:
    pass
after = len(os.listdir("/proc/self/fd"))
os.chmod = real_chmod
print(f"fd before={before} after={after} leaked={after - before}")
```

Observed:

```
fd before=9 after=10 leaked=1
```

Expected:
```
fd before=9 after=9 leaked=0 
```

## 2) `chmod` follows a replacement symlink

The swap below is what a concurrent directory writer can do in the window between `os.open` and `os.chmod`. This requires a concurrent writer with access to the destination directory; it is not a remote exploit.

```python
import errno
import os
import stat
import tempfile

import click

workdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
dest = os.path.join(workdir, "atomic-out.txt")
victim = os.path.join(workdir, "victim.txt")
with open(dest, "w") as f:
    f.write("dest\n")
with open(victim, "w") as f:
    f.write("secret\n")
os.chmod(dest, 0o644)
os.chmod(victim, 0o600)
print("victim before", oct(stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(victim).st_mode)))

real_chmod = os.chmod

def attack_chmod(path, mode, *args, **kwargs):
    path = os.fspath(path)
    if os.path.basename(path).startswith(".__atomic-write"):
        os.unlink(path)
        os.symlink(victim, path)
        real_chmod(path, mode, *args, **kwargs)
        print("victim after chmod", oct(stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(victim).st_mode)))
        raise OSError(errno.EPERM, "stop after chmod", path)
    return real_chmod(path, mode, *args, **kwargs)

os.chmod = attack_chmod
try:
    click.open_file(dest, "w", atomic=True)
except OSError:
    pass
os.chmod = real_chmod
print("victim final", oct(stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(victim).st_mode)))
```
Observed:

```
victim before 0o600
victim after chmod 0o644
victim final 0o644
```

Expected:
```
victim before 0o600
victim final 0o600
```

The victim file was never passed to `open_file`. Its mode changed because `os.chmod` followed the symlink.


## Environment:

- Python version: 3.12.3
- Click version: 8.5.1.dev

rows.title: `click.Path` should be generic on `path_type`
rows.body:
Click 8.5.0 made `click.prompt` and `click.ParamType` generic, so the return type of `click.prompt` is now normally clever enough to reveal the actual type of the value as converted from raw input.

However, `click.Path` has a `path_type` parameter to which the input is converted, but  that information is not reflected in the return type of `click.Path.convert`, so it's always typed as `str | bytes | os.PathLike[str]`, regardless of the value of `path_type`.

```python
# mre.py
import pathlib

from typing_extensions import assert_type

import click

my_type = click.Path(file_okay=False, path_type=pathlib.Path)
path = click.prompt("Enter a name", type=my_type)

# expected: pathlib.Path, actual: str | bytes | os.PathLike[str]
assert_type(path, pathlib.Path)
```

I checked the above MRE with mypy and pyright, as well as ty for completeness, on a local clone of the repo @ `main`:

```console
$ uv run mypy mre.py
mre.py:12: error: Expression is of type "str | bytes | PathLike[str]", not "Path"  [assert-type]
    assert_type(path, pathlib.Path)
    ^
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
```

```console
$ uv run pyright mre.py
WARNING: there is a new pyright version available (v1.1.408 -> v1.1.411).
Please install the new version or set PYRIGHT_PYTHON_FORCE_VERSION to `latest`

/Users/edgarramirez/Contrib/pallets/click/mre.py
  /Users/edgarramirez/Contrib/pallets/click/mre.py:12:13 - error: "assert_type" mismatch: expected "Path" but received "str | bytes | PathLike[str]" (reportAssertTypeFailure)
1 error, 0 warnings, 0 informations
```

```console
$ uv run ty check mre.py
error[type-assertion-failure]: Argument does not have asserted type `Path`
  --> mre.py:12:1
   |
12 | assert_type(path, pathlib.Path)
   | ^^^^^^^^^^^^----^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |             |
   |             Inferred type is `str | bytes | PathLike[str]`
info: `Path` and `str | bytes | PathLike[str]` are not equivalent types

Found 1 diagnostic
```

I expect the return type of `click.prompt` to match the `path_type` value passed to `click.Path`.

- Click version: 8.5.0

rows.title: [Bug] On Windows, get_pager_file returns a typing.BinaryIO object NOT typing.TextIO
rows.body:
Inside `src/click/_termui_impl.py`, the function `get_pager_file` delegates the creation of a tempfile to `_tempfilepager`, which returns a `BinaryIO` object of the opened file:

```python
f = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="wb", delete=False)
try:
    yield t.cast(t.BinaryIO, f), encoding, color
...
```
Which is called by _pager_contextmanager in
```python
...
if pager_cmd_parts:
        if WIN:
            return _tempfilepager(pager_cmd_parts, color)
        return _pipepager(pager_cmd_parts, color)
...
    if WIN or sys.platform.startswith("os2"):
        return _tempfilepager(["more"], color)
    return _pipepager(["less"], color)
```
In the end `get_pager_file`
```python
def get_pager_file(color: bool | None = None) -> t.Generator[t.TextIO, None, None]:
    ...
    with _pager_contextmanager(color=color) as (stream, encoding, color):
    # Split streams by capabilities rather than the abstract TextIO /
    # BinaryIO annotations: buffered text streams can be unwrapped to bytes,
    # while other streams are yielded as-is.
    wrapper: MaybeStripAnsi | None = None
        if _has_binary_buffer(stream):
            # Text stream backed by a binary buffer.
            wrapper = MaybeStripAnsi(stream.buffer, color=color, encoding=encoding)
            stream = wrapper
        try:
            # Narrow the BinaryIO | TextIO union that _pager_contextmanager
            # yields; the caller writes text to the pager.
            yield t.cast(t.TextIO, stream)
        ...
```
In the above `yield t.cast(t.TextIO, stream)` stream object will be `BinaryIO`, contradicting the `TextIO` annotation of the return value, all because it was created with the mode `"wb"` earlier.

Then if a caller tries: `stream.write("some text")` it will raise an exception:
`TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str'`

FIX:
In `_tempfilepager`, create the temp file with `mode='w'`
```python
f = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", delete=False)
```
I went ahead and created a pull request:
https://github.com/pallets/click/pull/3739

rows.title: echo_via_pager broken on Windows since 8.4.0
rows.body: Since the 8.4.0 pager rewrite, echo_via_pager on Windows dies with PermissionError WinError 32. Real cause: the temp file _tempfilepager yields has no .buffer, so str gets written to a binary handle (TypeError), then the finally tries to unlink the still-open file and Windows refuses. 8.3.3 works.

rows.title: echo_via_pager on Windows fails with WinError 32, masking a TypeError from writing str to a binary temp file (8.4.0 regression)
rows.body:
On Windows, `click.echo_via_pager()` fails with a `PermissionError: [WinError 32]` naming a temp file. The reported error is cleanup noise masking the real one: a `TypeError` from writing `str` into a binary-mode temp file.

Regression introduced in 8.4.0 by the `get_pager_file` / `_pager_contextmanager` rewrite. Reproduced on 8.4.0, 8.4.1, 8.4.2, and the code shape is unchanged on `main`.

Windows-only. `_pipepager`'s `Popen(..., text=True).stdin` is a `TextIOWrapper` with a real `.buffer`, so POSIX takes a different path and is unaffected.

### Cause

`_tempfilepager` yields a `NamedTemporaryFile(mode="wb")` to the caller:

```python
f = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="wb", delete=False)
try:
    yield t.cast(t.BinaryIO, f), encoding, color
```

`get_pager_file` then decides whether to wrap it for text writes:

```python
if _has_binary_buffer(stream):
    wrapper = MaybeStripAnsi(stream.buffer, color=color, encoding=encoding)
    stream = wrapper
```

`_has_binary_buffer` is `getattr(stream, "buffer", None) is not None`. A `NamedTemporaryFile` returns a `_TemporaryFileWrapper`, which has **no** `.buffer` attribute, so the check is False and the text wrapper is never installed. `echo_via_pager` then writes `str` directly to a binary handle:

```
TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str'
```

That exception unwinds into `_tempfilepager`'s cleanup:

```python
finally:
    os.unlink(f.name)
```

The handle is still open in the same process, and Windows will not unlink an open file, so `PermissionError` replaces the `TypeError` and becomes the only thing the user sees. Anyone hitting this will reasonably suspect antivirus or file locking rather than a type error.

Side effect of the same masking: when the paging path *does* succeed the file is closed first, so the `finally` is only reachable in a broken state.

### Reproduction

Needs a tty on stdin/stdout to reach `_tempfilepager`, so this forces the branch to stay runnable under captured stdio:

```python
import click
from click import _termui_impl as ti

ti.isatty = lambda stream: True
ti.WIN = True

click.echo_via_pager(f"line {i}\n" for i in range(50))
```

```
  File "click/termui.py", line 346, in echo_via_pager
    with get_pager_file(color=color) as pager:
  File "click/_termui_impl.py", line 633, in _tempfilepager
    os.unlink(f.name)
PermissionError: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process: 'C:\...\Temp\tmpsswp_chu'
```

On a real Windows terminal, no monkeypatching needed — any output taller than the window reproduces it. Surfacing the masked error:

```python
from click import _termui_impl as ti
gen = ti._tempfilepager(["cat"], color=False)
f, enc, color = gen.__enter__()
f.write("line\n")   # TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str'
```

### Downstream impact

Found via [mycli](https://github.com/dbcli/mycli) 2.7.0, which pins `click~=8.4.2` and calls `echo_via_pager` whenever query output exceeds the terminal. Any `SHOW TABLES` on a database with more tables than terminal rows dies with WinError 32. Pinning `click==8.3.3` is a clean workaround, since the pre-8.4 `_tempfilepager` buffered and encoded internally rather than yielding the handle.

### Suggested fix

Wrap the temp file so it both accepts `str` and satisfies the `.buffer` check, and close before unlinking:

```diff
-    f = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="wb", delete=False)
+    raw = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="wb", delete=False)
+    filename = raw.name
+    f = io.TextIOWrapper(raw, encoding=encoding)
     try:
-        yield t.cast(t.BinaryIO, f), encoding, color
-        f.flush()
-        f.close()
-        subprocess.call([str(cmd_path), f.name])
+        yield f, encoding, color
+        f.flush()
+        f.close()
+        subprocess.call([str(cmd_path), filename])
     finally:
-        os.unlink(f.name)
+        if not f.closed:
+            f.close()
+        os.unlink(filename)
```

Capturing `filename` up front matters because `f.name` is not reachable through the wrapper the same way. Guarding `f.close()` in the `finally` is what stops a mid-write exception from turning into WinError 32 and hiding itself.

Verified locally: `str` writes are accepted, the pager subprocess receives the content, and the unlink succeeds.

Two alternatives if you'd rather not change the yielded type:

- Have `_has_binary_buffer` also accept objects exposing a `file` attribute (`_TemporaryFileWrapper.file`), keeping the yield binary.
- Use `tempfile.mkstemp()` + `open(filename, "w", encoding=...)`, which sidesteps the wrapper class entirely.

### Environment

- Windows 11, Python 3.11
- click 8.4.0 / 8.4.1 / 8.4.2 all affected; 8.3.3 not affected
- `PAGER` unset and set to `less` both reproduce; `less` present on PATH

## Description

Sentinel is an enum where each member is initialized with a unique object() value. The whole purpose of using object() rather than a plain sentinel like None or a string is identity-based comparison and the guarantee that no user-provided value can collide with it. This is load-bearing behavior: Option.consume_value and many other call sites use `is UNSET` / `== UNSET` checks. No tests verify that the two members are distinct from each other, from None, from empty strings, or from arbitrary objects passed by users.

rows.title: confirmation_prompt with a non-empty default loops forever (default can never be confirmed)
rows.body:
### Describe the bug

When `click.prompt()` (or `@click.option(prompt=..., confirmation_prompt=True, default=...)`) has `confirmation_prompt=True` **and a non-empty `default`**, pressing Enter to accept the shown default can never be confirmed — the confirmation prompt repeats forever.

The empty-input special case added in #2158 ("allow empty str input for prompt") tests `value` *after* it has already been reassigned to the default, so it only fires when the default itself is falsy (`""`). Any non-empty default loops.

### Reproduce

```python
import click
from click.testing import CliRunner

@click.command()
@click.option("--password", prompt=True, confirmation_prompt=True, default="sekret")
def cli(password):
    click.echo(f"RESULT={password}")

result = CliRunner().invoke(cli, input="\n\n", standalone_mode=False)  # Enter, Enter
print(repr(result.output))
```

Observed: `Password [sekret]: ` then `Repeat for confirmation: ` repeated → `Abort()` (a real terminal re-prompts forever). By contrast, `default=""` with `\n\n` correctly returns `""`.

### Expected

Pressing Enter at both prompts accepts the default (`RESULT=sekret`), consistent with the documented empty-string-default behavior from #2158.

### Environment

- Click, `main` (8.5.0.dev0)

I have a fix + regression test ready and will open a PR.

rows.title: 8.4.x: prompt/confirm(err=True) leaks prompt tail and CliRunner reply echo to stdout on Windows
rows.body:
On the stable 8.4.x line, `prompt()` / `confirm()` with `err=True` still write part of the prompt interaction to **stdout** on Windows, because `_readline_prompt`'s `WIN` branch bypasses the stderr redirect that the POSIX branch applies:

```python
# src/click/termui.py (8.4.2)
def _readline_prompt(func, text, err):
    if WIN:
        echo(text[:-1], nl=False, err=err)   # prompt body honors err ...
        return func(text[-1:])               # ... but this call is NOT redirected
    if err:
        with redirect_stdout(sys.stderr):    # POSIX: fully redirected
            return func(text)
    return func(text)
```

Consequences on Windows only:

1. **Real console**: `input(text[-1:])` writes the prompt's last character (the trailing space of `"... [y/N]: "`) to stdout. For CLIs that promise "stdout is a single machine-readable document" under a `--json` flag (prompt chrome on stderr via `err=True`), that's a stray byte in the payload stream — benign for JSON parsers since it's whitespace, but the contract is broken.
2. **`CliRunner`** (the bigger practical hit): test isolation replaces `termui.visible_prompt_func` with a shim that echoes the prompt tail **and the typed reply** to `sys.stdout`. Because the `WIN` branch doesn't wrap the call in `redirect_stdout`, stdout becomes `" n\n" + <payload>`. Any test doing `json.loads(result.stdout)` on a prompt-then-JSON flow passes on POSIX and fails on Windows with `Expecting value: line 1 column 2 (char 1)`.

## Reproduction

Deterministic on a Windows runner; on POSIX you can force the branch to see the exact same behavior:

```python
import json
import click, click.termui
from click.testing import CliRunner

@click.command()
def cmd():
    if not click.confirm("Continue?", default=False, err=True):
        click.echo(json.dumps({"ok": False}))

# click.termui.WIN = True   # <- uncomment on POSIX to simulate
result = CliRunner().invoke(cmd, [], input="n\n")
print(repr(result.stdout))
# POSIX / main:  '{"ok": false}\n'
# Windows 8.4.2: ' n\n{"ok": false}\n'
```

Environment: click 8.4.2, Python 3.12, observed on GitHub Actions `windows-latest` (and reproduced via the `WIN = True` simulation above on macOS/Linux).

## Note on main

This is already fixed on `main` as a side effect of the colorama removal (74546476376b39d05186ec1085fd2faf9d86fa20) — `_readline_prompt` no longer has a `WIN` branch, so the `err=True` redirect applies on all platforms. So this report is effectively a request to consider backporting the redirect part to the 8.4.x stable line (the `if WIN:` branch could keep the separate `echo` for coloring but wrap the `func` call in `redirect_stdout(sys.stderr)` when `err=True`).

Downstream context, if useful: this surfaced as two Windows-only CI failures in memtomem (bisect + analysis in https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem/issues/1640); we've since worked around it by bypassing the prompt machinery for our `--json` paths.

rows.title: Automatically append ellipsis (`...`) to metavars when `multiple=True` in options
rows.body:
When building a command-line interface with `click.option(..., multiple=True)`, the auto-generated usage string does not visually signal to the user that the option can be repeated. For instance, an option --foo=FOO looks identical whether it accepts single or multiple arguments. This is different from the common convention for multi-value items in shell interfaces often suggests adding an ellipsis like `--foo=FOO...`

Expected behavior if option "foo" has `multiple=True`:
```
Usage: script.py [OPTIONS]

Options:
  --foo TEXT...  A list of foo strings.
  --help         Show this message and exit.
```

rows.title: Native colorized help text
rows.body:
It is still not easy to add colors to help text with click in default configuration, considering that click has always supported stylized echo. There was a ticket that someone opened 10+ years ago (#269), which others then suggested to use the [click-help-colors](https://github.com/r-m-n/click-help-colors) extension. Problem is that it has been out of maintenance for 2 years with no sign of recovery, and depends on deprecated features scheduled to be removed on release of click 9.0.

Also with Python 3.14, argparse now [adds color to its generated help text](https://docs.python.org/3/library/argparse.html#argumentparser-objects) *by default*. Adding all of the above together, maybe it's time to reconsider adding native support of colorized help text to click? IMO it doesn't have to be as customizable as the click-help-colors did, just some sensible defaults with the possibility to override the palette for each type of options/arguments would suffice. This would also align with the project's philosophy of "creating beautiful command line interfaces in a composable way with as little code as necessary".

rows.title: FloatRange with clamp=True returns int when the boundary was given as an int
rows.body:
`FloatRange` is documented to convert values to `float`, but when `clamp=True` is used and the boundary was given as an `int`, clamping returns the boundary as an `int` instead of a `float`.

### Minimal reproducible example

```python
import click

ft = click.FloatRange(0, 1, clamp=True)

print(repr(ft.convert("2.5", None, None)))   # 1   (expected 1.0)
print(type(ft.convert("2.5", None, None)))   # <class 'int'>   (expected float)

print(repr(ft.convert("-2.5", None, None)))  # 0   (expected 0.0)
print(type(ft.convert("-2.5", None, None)))  # <class 'int'>   (expected float)
```

In-range values are unaffected because they pass through `float()`:

```python
print(type(ft.convert("0.5", None, None)))   # <class 'float'>  (correct)
```

The bug only appears when the boundary literal is an `int`. Passing float
literals masks it:

```python
print(type(click.FloatRange(0.0, 1.0, clamp=True).convert("2.5", None, None)))
# <class 'float'>  (correct, but only because the bound was a float)
```

### Expected behavior

`FloatRange.convert` should always return a `float`, regardless of how the
boundary literals were written. Returning an `int` here breaks downstream
code that relies on the documented return type (e.g. JSON serialization that
distinguishes `1` from `1.0`, `isinstance(x, int)` checks, or arithmetic that
behaves differently for `int` vs `float`).

`IntRange` is not affected; its clamped result is correctly an `int`.

### Root cause

`FloatRange._clamp` returns the stored boundary (`self.min` / `self.max`)
directly for non-open bounds. Those are kept exactly as the user passed them
to the constructor, so an `int` literal stays an `int`.

Environment:

- Python version: 3.12
- Click version: 8.5.0.dev0 (current `main`)

rows.title: fish completion is broken in 8.4.1
rows.body:
Commit 19fd4d6 (#3126) broke fish completion.

## Unquoted `\n`

```diff
-        set -l metadata (string split "," $completion);
+        set -l metadata (string split \n $completion);
```
Without quotes, `\n` is evaluated as a literal newline, which splits the command across lines in the generated script:
```
        set -l metadata (string split
 $completion);
```

## Command substitution flattens newlines

Even if quoted, `\n` fails as a separator. The Python side outputs:
```python
        return f"{item.type}\n{value}\n{help_escaped}"
```
But when captured via command substitution in Fish, the newlines are flattened:
```fish
    set -l response (env %(complete_var)s=fish_complete COMP_WORDS=(commandline -cp) \
COMP_CWORD=(commandline -t) %(prog_name)s);
```

---

To support multi-line, maybe we just need to escape `\n` in help message while keeping the old separator? Not 100% sure.

Either way, we should probably revert this change first to fix the broken completion

rows.title: Advanced Patterns example uses Python 2 `urllib.urlopen`
rows.body:
The examples in the **"Parameter Modifications"** section of the *Advanced Patterns* guide (`docs/advanced.md`) use `urllib.urlopen(...)`, which is a Python 2 API. It was removed in Python 3, where the function lives at `urllib.request.urlopen`.

### Where

Page: https://click.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/advanced/#parameter-modifications
Source: `docs/advanced.md`, "Parameter Modifications" section.

```python
import urllib

def open_url(ctx, param, value):
    if value is not None:
        ctx.params['fp'] = urllib.urlopen(value)
    return value
```

The same `urllib.urlopen` call also appears in the second example of that section.

### Reproduce

Copy the snippet and run it on any Python 3 interpreter:

```pycon
>>> import urllib
>>> urllib.urlopen("https://example.com")
AttributeError: module 'urllib' has no attribute 'urlopen'
```

### Expected

The examples should use `import urllib.request` and `urllib.request.urlopen(value)`, so they run on the supported Python versions.

### Also (minor wording)

In the **"Forwarding Unknown Options"** section, one sentence reads:

> If the command would be **ignored** with `-va` then the `-v` part would be handled by Click ...

Given the context (the `-v` option *is* recognized and handled), this should read "**invoked** with `-va`".

I'd be happy to open a PR with these changes.

Environment:

- Python version: any 3.x
- Click version: docs on `main` (and current stable docs)

```shell
    file.write(out)  # type: ignore
```

```diff
    if nl:
```

rows.title: _pipepager mis-detects raw-mode flag, enabling color from any 'r'/'R' substring in $LESS or filename args
rows.body:
## Summary

`_pipepager` in `src/click/_termui_impl.py` mis-detects whether the user requested raw control characters (`-r`/`-R`) when deciding to enable colored output. Two distinct bugs combine in the same expression (lines ~488–493):

```python
less_flags = f"{os.environ.get('LESS', '')}{' '.join(cmd_params)}"
if not less_flags:
    env["LESS"] = "-R"
    color = True
elif "r" in less_flags or "R" in less_flags:
    color = True
```

### Bug 1 — substring check yields false positives

`"r" in less_flags` matches **any** occurrence of the letter `r`/`R` in either the env var or the CLI args, not just the `-r`/`-R` flag. Concretely:

- `pager.echo_via_pager(..., color=None)` invoked while `$PAGER="less"` and the user runs `less README.md` → enables color (because `README.md` contains `R`).
- `$LESS="--prompt=resume"` (a documented `less` option) → enables color.
- `$LESS="--mouse"` plus `less requirements.txt` → enables color (filename contains `r`).

### Bug 2 — env var and CLI args are concatenated without a separator

The expression `f"{os.environ.get('LESS', '')}{' '.join(cmd_params)}"` joins the env value and the args with no boundary character, so neither half can be parsed back out for any subsequent decision. It also means a value spanning the join (e.g. `$LESS="-X"` plus `cmd_params=["README.md"]`) yields `"-XREADME.md"`, where `R` from the filename is treated as if it came from `$LESS`.

The intent appears to be: **inspect parsed flags from both sources**, not substring-match an unstructured concatenation.

## Reproduction

Save as `reproduce_pager_bugs.py` at the click repo root and run with `python3 reproduce_pager_bugs.py`. It monkey-patches `subprocess.Popen` so no real pager is launched, then drives `_pipepager(cmd_parts, color=None)` and reports the resolved `color` value.

```python
"""Reproduction for two bugs in click/_termui_impl.py::_pipepager around line 488."""

import os, sys, subprocess
from unittest.mock import patch
from io import BytesIO

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "src"))
from click._termui_impl import _pipepager


class FakePopen:
    def __init__(self, argv, *, env=None, **kw):
        self.argv, self.env, self.stdin = argv, env, BytesIO()
    def communicate(self): return (b"", b"")
    def wait(self): return 0
    def terminate(self): pass


def run_case(label, cmd_parts, less_env=None):
    saved = os.environ.get("LESS")
    if less_env is None: os.environ.pop("LESS", None)
    else: os.environ["LESS"] = less_env
    try:
        with patch.object(subprocess, "Popen", FakePopen):
            with _pipepager(cmd_parts, color=None) as (_s, _e, color):
                pass
            print(f"  {label}: cmd_parts={cmd_parts!r} $LESS={less_env!r} -> color={color!r}")
    finally:
        if saved is None: os.environ.pop("LESS", None)
        else: os.environ["LESS"] = saved


import shutil
if not shutil.which("less"):
    print("less(1) not on PATH; skipping.")
    sys.exit(0)

print("=== Expected color=False (filename, not -R flag) ===")
run_case("less README.md", ["less", "README.md"])
run_case("less requirements.txt", ["less", "requirements.txt"])

print("\n=== Expected color=False ($LESS used for unrelated option) ===")
run_case("less, $LESS=--prompt=resume", ["less"], less_env="--prompt=resume")

print("\n=== Controls (already correct) ===")
run_case("less -X", ["less", "-X"])
run_case("less -R", ["less", "-R"])
```

### Output on current `main` (`fc6c7c47`):

```
=== Expected color=False (filename, not -R flag) ===
  less README.md: cmd_parts=['less', 'README.md'] $LESS=None -> color=True
  less requirements.txt: cmd_parts=['less', 'requirements.txt'] $LESS=None -> color=True

=== Expected color=False ($LESS used for unrelated option) ===
  less, $LESS=--prompt=resume: cmd_parts=['less'] $LESS='--prompt=resume' -> color=True

=== Controls (already correct) ===
  less -X: cmd_parts=['less', '-X'] $LESS=None -> color=False
  less -R: cmd_parts=['less', '-R'] $LESS=None -> color=True
```

The first three cases should report `color=False` and instead report `True`.

## Impact

Click writes ANSI escapes to the pager whenever this triggers. With `less` being invoked in a default mode (no `-R`/`-r`), those escapes display as literal `^[[31m...` sequences instead of color, making output noisier than no-color mode would be. Severity is low (cosmetic), but the bug is silent and triggers in very ordinary invocations like `cli --help | less README.md`-style flows or any `$PAGER` setup that includes a path with an `r`.

## Suggested fix

Inspect parsed tokens from both sources, not a concatenated substring. Roughly:

```python
def _less_uses_raw_mode(less_env: str, cmd_params: list[str]) -> bool:
    import shlex
    tokens = shlex.split(less_env) + cmd_params
    for tok in tokens:
        # Only short-flag bundles like -R, -rX, -XrY count; long options
        # and filenames do not.
        if tok.startswith("-") and not tok.startswith("--") and len(tok) > 1:
            if "r" in tok[1:] or "R" in tok[1:]:
                return True
    return False
```

The two empty-input cases (no `$LESS` and no `cmd_params`) keep the existing behavior of injecting `LESS=-R` and enabling color.

I'm happy to send a PR with the fix + a regression test mirroring the reproduction above if that's welcome.

## Environment

- Click: current `main` at commit `fc6c7c47`
- Python: 3.14.4
- macOS 14, `less` from system path


### Bug 1 — substring check yields false positives

`"r" in less_flags` matches **any** occurrence of the letter `r`/`R` in either the env var or the CLI args, not just the `-r`/`-R` flag. Concretely:

- `pager.echo_via_pager(..., color=None)` invoked while `$PAGER="less"` and the user runs `less README.md` → enables color (because `README.md` contains `R`).
- `$LESS="--prompt=resume"` (a documented `less` option) → enables color.
- `$LESS="--mouse"` plus `less requirements.txt` → enables color (filename contains `r`).

### Bug 2 — env var and CLI args are concatenated without a separator

The expression `f"{os.environ.get('LESS', '')}{' '.join(cmd_params)}"` joins the env value and the args with no boundary character, so neither half can be parsed back out for any subsequent decision. It also means a value spanning the join (e.g. `$LESS="-X"` plus `cmd_params=["README.md"]`) yields `"-XREADME.md"`, where `R` from the filename is treated as if it came from `$LESS`.

The intent appears to be: **inspect parsed flags from both sources**, not substring-match an unstructured concatenation.

## Reproduction

Save as `reproduce_pager_bugs.py` at the click repo root and run with `python3 reproduce_pager_bugs.py`. It monkey-patches `subprocess.Popen` so no real pager is launched, then drives `_pipepager(cmd_parts, color=None)` and reports the resolved `color` value.

```python
"""Reproduction for two bugs in click/_termui_impl.py::_pipepager around line 488."""

import os, sys, subprocess
from unittest.mock import patch
from io import BytesIO

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "src"))
from click._termui_impl import _pipepager


class FakePopen:
    def __init__(self, argv, *, env=None, **kw):
        self.argv, self.env, self.stdin = argv, env, BytesIO()
    def communicate(self): return (b"", b"")
    def wait(self): return 0
    def terminate(self): pass


def run_case(label, cmd_parts, less_env=None):
    saved = os.environ.get("LESS")
    if less_env is None: os.environ.pop("LESS", None)
    else: os.environ["LESS"] = less_env
    try:
        with patch.object(subprocess, "Popen", FakePopen):
            with _pipepager(cmd_parts, color=None) as (_s, _e, color):
                pass
            print(f"  {label}: cmd_parts={cmd_parts!r} $LESS={less_env!r} -> color={color!r}")
    finally:
        if saved is None: os.environ.pop("LESS", None)
        else: os.environ["LESS"] = saved


import shutil
if not shutil.which("less"):
    print("less(1) not on PATH; skipping.")
    sys.exit(0)

print("=== Expected color=False (filename, not -R flag) ===")
run_case("less README.md", ["less", "README.md"])
run_case("less requirements.txt", ["less", "requirements.txt"])

print("\n=== Expected color=False ($LESS used for unrelated option) ===")
run_case("less, $LESS=--prompt=resume", ["less"], less_env="--prompt=resume")

print("\n=== Controls (already correct) ===")
run_case("less -X", ["less", "-X"])
run_case("less -R", ["less", "-R"])
```

### Output on current `main` (`fc6c7c47`):

```
=== Expected color=False (filename, not -R flag) ===
  less README.md: cmd_parts=['less', 'README.md'] $LESS=None -> color=True
  less requirements.txt: cmd_parts=['less', 'requirements.txt'] $LESS=None -> color=True

=== Expected color=False ($LESS used for unrelated option) ===
  less, $LESS=--prompt=resume: cmd_parts=['less'] $LESS='--prompt=resume' -> color=True

=== Controls (already correct) ===
  less -X: cmd_parts=['less', '-X'] $LESS=None -> color=False
  less -R: cmd_parts=['less', '-R'] $LESS=None -> color=True
```

The first three cases should report `color=False` and instead report `True`.

## Impact

Click writes ANSI escapes to the pager whenever this triggers. With `less` being invoked in a default mode (no `-R`/`-r`), those escapes display as literal `^[[31m...` sequences instead of color, making output noisier than no-color mode would be. Severity is low (cosmetic), but the bug is silent and triggers in very ordinary invocations like `cli --help | less README.md`-style flows or any `$PAGER` setup that includes a path with an `r`.

## Suggested fix

Inspect parsed tokens from both sources, not a concatenated substring. Roughly:

```python
def _less_uses_raw_mode(less_env: str, cmd_params: list[str]) -> bool:
    import shlex
    tokens = shlex.split(less_env) + cmd_params
    for tok in tokens:
        # Only short-flag bundles like -R, -rX, -XrY count; long options
        # and filenames do not.
        if tok.startswith("-") and not tok.startswith("--") and len(tok) > 1:
            if "r" in tok[1:] or "R" in tok[1:]:
                return True
    return False
```

The two empty-input cases (no `$LESS` and no `cmd_params`) keep the existing behavior of injecting `LESS=-R` and enabling color.

I'm happy to send a PR with the fix + a regression test mirroring the reproduction above if that's welcome.

## Environment

- Click: current `main` at commit `fc6c7c47`
- Python: 3.14.4
- macOS 14, `less` from system path

rows.title: "default" behaviour in Click 8.3.x changes with enable/disable boolean flag pair
rows.body:
In click 8.2.1, defining a boolean option with both a "enable" and "disable" flag option works with the following logic:
```
import click

@click.command("foo")
@click.option("--without-xyz", "enable_xyz", flag_value=False)
@click.option("--with-xyz", "enable_xyz", flag_value=True, default=True)
def foo(enable_xyz):
    print(f"enable_xyz = {enable_xyz}")

foo()
```

With this code, using click 8.2.1:
* `python foo.py --with-xyz` returns True
* `python foo.py --without-xyz` returns False
* `python foo.py --with-xyz --without-xyz` returns False
* `python foo.py --without-xyz --with-xyz` returns True
* `python foo.py` returns False

In click 8.3.0, the output is the same for every case except the "default"  case - `python foo.py` returns True.

This is an extension of #3111; this [pattern is used in MkDocs](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/blob/2862536793b3c67d9d83c33e0dd6d50a791928f8/mkdocs/__main__.py#L257) (as of MkDocs 1.6.1) (see mkdocs/mkdocs#4032).

However, the fix for #3111 (#3239) doesn't fix this edge case.

The Properdocs fork of MkDocs [has worked around the issue](https://github.com/ProperDocs/properdocs/pull/14/files).

Environment:

- Python version: 3.12, 3.13, 3.14
- Click version: 8.3.0, 8.3.3

rows.title: Click 8.3.3 breaks `pytest` when stream `fd` is duplicated
rows.body:
Starting from Click 8.3.3, I've noticed that it breaks pytest when the standard stream is duplicated with `os.dup2`.

I guess the related change is: https://github.com/pallets/click/pull/3244

I am not sure if this is an expected behaviro of that change, but for me it was a bit surprising behavior, hence reporting.

__Reproducer__

```python
"""
Passes on click <=8.3.2, crashes pytest on click 8.3.3.

    pip install click==8.3.3 pytest
    pytest test_click_fileno_regression.py  # OSError: Illegal seek

    pip install click==8.3.2
    pytest test_click_fileno_regression.py   # passes
"""

import io
import os
import sys

import click
from click.testing import CliRunner


@click.command()
def cmd():
    # Many libraries (build tools, logging tees, subprocess wrappers)
    # use os.dup2 on sys.stdout.fileno() to redirect output at the
    # fd level.
    #
    # On click <=8.3.2, sys.stdout.fileno() inside CliRunner raises
    # UnsupportedOperation.
    #
    # On click 8.3.3, sys.stdout.fileno() returns the original
    # stream's fd
    try:
        stdout_fd = sys.stdout.fileno()
    except io.UnsupportedOperation:
        click.echo("fileno() not available (click <=8.3.2)")
        return

    r, w = os.pipe()
    os.dup2(w, stdout_fd)
    os.close(w)
    os.close(r)
    click.echo("hello")


def test_invoke():
    runner = CliRunner()
    result = runner.invoke(cmd)
    assert result.exit_code == 0
```

rows.title: `HelpFormatter.write_usage` breaks options at a hyphen
rows.body:
If an option containing a hyphen in its name is printed at the line break limit, it’s broken at the hyphen.

### Reproduction

```python
import click

options = [
    "--enable-verbose-logging",
    "--output-file-path",
    "--max-retry-count",
    "--disable-cache-mode",
    "--config-file-location",
    "--user-auth-token",
    "--auto-update-interval",
    "--force-overwrite-existing",
    "--network-timeout-seconds",
    "--debug-trace-enabled",
]

f = click.HelpFormatter(width=65)
f.write_usage("program", " ".join(options))
print(f.getvalue())
```

### Expected output
```
Usage: program --enable-verbose-logging --output-file-path
               --max-retry-count --disable-cache-mode
               --config-file-location --user-auth-token
               --auto-update-interval --force-overwrite-existing
               --network-timeout-seconds --debug-trace-enabled
```

### Actual output
```
Usage: program --enable-verbose-logging --output-file-path --max-
               retry-count --disable-cache-mode --config-file-
               location --user-auth-token --auto-update-interval
               --force-overwrite-existing --network-timeout-
               seconds --debug-trace-enabled
```

### Environment

- Python version: 3.12.3
- Click version: 8.3.1

### Additional information

#### `width` option

This also happens without specifying `width`. The `width` option is altered in the example to make the issue more frequent.

#### Relevance to other use cases

This may likely only affect:

- direct users of `click.HelpFormatter`,
- users of `click.argument` with custom `metavar` containing hyphens. 

On the other hand, `click` prints `[OPTIONS]` instead of listing individual options on the usage line and uses underscores instead of hyphens in argument names (unless specifying `metavar`).

#### Cause

I looked into the code and found that `textwrap.TextWrapper` is used under the hood, which has the [`break_on_hyphens`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/textwrap.html#textwrap.TextWrapper.break_on_hyphens) option. However, there is no option for the `click` user to influence this, apart from reimplementing `HelpFormatter.write_usage` (in a subclass) and `wrap_text`.

rows.title: Generates broken completions for mac with bash 3
rows.body:
# Bash completion uses `complete -o nosort` unconditionally, breaks on bash < 4.4

## Environment

- macOS 15 (Sequoia / Tahoe), Apple Silicon
- Bash 3.2.57(1)-release (macOS default shell)
- check-jsonschema 0.37.1 installed via Homebrew
- bash-completion v1 (1.3_3)

## Description

The generated bash completion script for Click-based tools uses `complete -o nosort` unconditionally. The `nosort` option for `complete` was introduced in bash 4.4. On macOS, the default shell is bash 3.2, which produces an error at every interactive login:

```
-bash: complete: nosort: invalid option name
```

The offending line in the installed completion script (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/check-jsonschema/0.37.1/etc/bash_completion.d/check-jsonschema`):

```bash
complete -o nosort -F _check_jsonschema_completion check-jsonschema
```

Click's own source acknowledges this requirement but doesn't act on it:

```python
# Only Bash >= 4.4 has the nosort option.
    complete -o nosort -F %(complete_func)s %(prog_name)s
```

## Expected behaviour

The generated completion should guard the `nosort` option behind a version check, e.g.:

```bash
if ((BASH_VERSINFO[0] > 4 || (BASH_VERSINFO[0] == 4 && BASH_VERSINFO[1] >= 4))); then
    complete -o nosort -F _check_jsonschema_completion check-jsonschema
else
    complete -F _check_jsonschema_completion check-jsonschema
fi
```

## Impact

This error fires on every new interactive shell on any macOS system using the default bash and bash-completion v1. Every Click-based CLI tool installed via Homebrew with a completion script will have the same problem.

## Comparison with other tools

Other Homebrew-installed tools with bash completion (`podman`, `yq`, `gh`, `helm`) avoid this issue by using `compopt -o nosort` inside the completion function body rather than `complete -o nosort` at registration time. `compopt` only executes during active tab completion, so it is never reached on shells that don't support it. All four tools were confirmed to complete correctly on bash 3.2.57.

The distinction:

- `complete -o nosort -F func cmd` — executes at source time when the completion script is loaded. **Breaks bash < 4.4.**
- `compopt -o nosort` inside the completion function — executes only during tab completion. **Safe on bash < 4.4** (never reached if the shell doesn't support it).

## Where to file

- **Primary (root cause):** https://github.com/pallets/click/issues — Click generates the completion script template.
- **Secondary (awareness):** https://github.com/python-jsonschema/check-jsonschema/issues — their Homebrew formula ships the broken output.

rows.title: FloatRange accepts NaN, bypassing range validation
rows.body:
## Bug

`click.FloatRange` accepts `NaN` as a valid value, bypassing range validation entirely. In contrast, `inf` and `-inf` are correctly rejected.

## Reproduction

```python
import click
from click.testing import CliRunner

@click.command()
@click.option("--temperature", type=click.FloatRange(-50.0, 150.0))
def cmd(temperature):
    click.echo(f"Processing: {temperature}C")

runner = CliRunner()

# NaN passes validation (bug)
result = runner.invoke(cmd, ["--temperature", "nan"])
print(result.exit_code)  # 0 — should be 2
print(result.output)     # "Processing: nanC"

# inf is correctly rejected
result = runner.invoke(cmd, ["--temperature", "inf"])
print(result.exit_code)  # 2 — correct
```

## Root cause

`_NumberRangeBase.convert` checks `rv < min` and `rv > max`. Since `NaN < 0.0` and `NaN > 1.0` both evaluate to `False`, the check `lt_min or gt_max` is `False`, so NaN passes through.

This also bypasses `clamp=True` — the NaN value is returned unclamped.

## Impact

Any CLI using `FloatRange` for input validation (temperature ranges, ratios, sensor data thresholds) will accept NaN and pass it to downstream code, where it silently corrupts calculations. The whole point of `FloatRange` is to reject invalid values, and NaN is not a valid number for any range.

## Environment

click 8.3.2, Python 3.12

rows.title: semver.Version as default causing an error
rows.body:
Any instance of `semver.Version` set as `default` in an option will lead to an error when Click tries to show it in the help text.
The problem seems to be that `Version` allows comparison to strings, and Click, when building the help text, tries to check the default value against an empty string `""`, which cannot be parsed by `semver.Version`:

```
  File ".venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/click/core.py", line 3091, in get_help_extra
    elif default_value == "":
         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/semver/version.py", line 52, in wrapper
    return operator(self, other)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/semver/version.py", line 467, in __eq__
    return self.compare(other) == 0
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/semver/version.py", line 394, in compare
    other = cls.parse(other)
            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/semver/version.py", line 644, in parse
    raise ValueError(f"{version} is not valid SemVer string")
ValueError:  is not valid SemVer string
```

This can be replicated with the following code by trying to print the help text:

<details>

```python
import click
from semver import Version


class SemverType(click.ParamType):
    name = "semver"

    def convert(self, value: str | Version, param: click.Parameter | None, ctx: click.Context | None) -> Version:
        if isinstance(value, Version):
            return value

        try:
            return Version.parse(value)
        except ValueError as e:
            raise self.fail(str(e), param, ctx) from e


@click.command()
@click.option(
    "--version",
    type=SemverType(),
    default=Version(1, 0, 0),
    show_default=True,
)
def cli(version: Version | None) -> None:
    print(version)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    cli()
```

</details>

By quickly inspecting the code, I'd say this could be fixed by checking whether `default_value` is actually a string before comparing it to `""`. 

Environment:

- Python version: 3.12
- Click version: 8.3.1
- semver version: 3.0.4

rows.title: Boolean flag envvar parsing treats non-empty values as true for is_flag options
rows.body:
## Summary

For a boolean flag option using `is_flag=True` with `envvar=...`, any non-empty env var value appears to activate the flag.

Observed behavior:
- `DRY_RUN=""` or unset => `False`
- `DRY_RUN="true"` => `True` (expected)
- `DRY_RUN="false"` => `True` (unexpected)
- `DRY_RUN="0"` => `True` (unexpected)
- `DRY_RUN="no"` => `True` (unexpected)

This seems inconsistent with docs that describe true/false token parsing for env vars on flags:
https://click.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/options/#values-from-environment-variables

## Reproducer

```python
import click

@click.command()
@click.option("--dry-run", is_flag=True, envvar="DRY_RUN")
def cli(dry_run):
    print(f"dry_run={dry_run!r}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    cli()
```

Run:

```bash
DRY_RUN=false python repro.py
```

Actual:

```text
dry_run=True
```

Expected:

```text
dry_run=False
```

## Versions tested

- Click 8.2.1
- Click 8.3.0
- Click 8.3.1

All showed same behavior in my test environment.

## Notes

Issue #2952/changelog mention envvar parsing fixes in 8.2.2, so this may be:
- a remaining edge case,
- a regression,
- or docs not matching current implementation for this option shape.

## Bug Description
`click.launch()` is broken on Windows in version 8.1.8. The migration from `os.system` to `subprocess.call` uses incorrect argument format for URLs, causing `WinError 2: The system cannot find the file specified`.

The `subprocess.call` invocation does not properly handle the `start` command on Windows when opening URLs.

`click.launch()` should open URLs on Windows without errors, as it did in 8.1.7.

rows.body:
Summary

It would be helpful to have a built‑in option or flag that lets Click output errors (help messages or exceptions) in JSON format. This would make it easier to integrate Click‑based CLIs into tools that parse machine output (e.g., logging services, automated testers).

Motivation

Currently, Click prints error messages in plain text. For some use cases — especially automated workflows, CI systems, and integrations — having an optional JSON representation of errors and help text would:

Make error parsing easier (no need for custom regex)

Support structured logging tools

Help when building higher‑level tooling around Click‑based CLIs

Proposal

Add a global option such as:

--format json

When provided, error output (and possibly help output) should be formatted in JSON, e.g.:
{
  "error": "Invalid option '--countt'",
  "code": 2,
  "help": null
}

This feature could also be limited to errors first, with structured help later.

Example usage
mycli --format json --countt 5

Expected output:

{
  "error": "No such option: --countt",
  "code": 2
}
Benefits

Helps with integrations and tooling

Encourages consistent, structured output

Optional and backward‑compatible

rows.title: AttributeError in make_default_short_help(None)
rows.body:
## Bug Description

`click.utils.make_default_short_help()` crashes with `AttributeError` when passed `None`. This can occur when programmatically creating commands where help text might not be provided, or when a developer passes `None` expecting the function to handle it gracefully.

## Reproduction

```python
from click.utils import make_default_short_help

# This crashes
result = make_default_short_help(None)
```

**Full traceback:**
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "click/utils.py", line 62, in make_default_short_help
    paragraph_end = help.find("\n\n")
                    ^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'find'
```

**Real-world scenario where this could happen:**
```python
@click.command()
@click.option('--help-text', default=None)
def my_command(help_text):
    # If help_text is None, this crashes
    short_help = make_default_short_help(help_text)
```

## Expected Behavior

The function should either:
1. Return an empty string (`""`) when passed `None`, OR
2. Raise a clear `TypeError` with a message like `"help must be a string, not NoneType"`

Currently, the `AttributeError` doesn't clearly indicate that the problem is with the input validation.

## Suggested Fix

Add input validation at the start of the function:

```python
def make_default_short_help(help: str | None, max_length: int = 45) -> str:
    if help is None:
        return ""
    # ... rest of function
```

Environment:

- Python version: 3.13.1
- Click version: latest from main branch (tested with git clone)

rows.title: Native Carapace Support
rows.body:
What is Carapace: https://carapace.sh/

From my understanding, it is kind of a Rosetta Stone, we write a single yaml file on how the command should complete, and it does its magic on working on multiple shells. (Bash, Cmd, Elvish, Fish, Nushell, Oil, Powershell, Tcsh, Xonsh, Zsh)

It does already have a bridge to work with Click:
https://github.com/carapace-sh/carapace-bridge/blob/master/pkg/actions/bridge/click.go
https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-bin/spec/bridge.html#click
(the amount of bridges to frameworks made me quite surprised of the comprehensive scope of the Carapace project)

So, from my tests, a software written with click does work the autocomplete, but the autocomplete is way too simple, or maybe I'm doing something wrong.

Anyway, I did found the Carapace documentation a bit confusing at first and it took me a while to find myself around it.

To summarize it a bit, Carapace has a Go-lang library offering native support. For non-Golang software, our option is to offer a yaml spec file that should be stored at: 
https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-bin/setup/userConfigDir.html

Linux/Unix:
`{XDG_CONFIG_HOME}/carapace/specs/{app}.yaml`
`{$HOME}/.config/carapace/specs/{app}.yaml`

Apple: `$HOME/Library/Application Support/carapace/specs/{app}.yaml`
Windows: `%AppData%\carapace\specs\{app}.yaml`
Plan 9: `$home/lib/carapace/specs/{app}.yaml`

We can get the current used spec for any command (to learn from examples) by using the command:
`carapace {app_name} spec`

example: `carapace adb spec`
```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://carapace.sh/schemas/command.json
name: adb
description: Android Debug Bridge
flags:
    -H: name of adb server host [default=localhost]
    -L=: listen on given socket for adb server [default=tcp:localhost:5037]
    -P: port of adb server [default=5037]
    -a: listen on all network interfaces, not just localhost
    -d: use USB device (error if multiple devices connected)
    -e: use TCP/IP device (error if multiple TCP/IP devices available)
    -s=: use device with given serial (overrides $ANDROID_SERIAL)
    -t=: use device with given transport id
commands:
    - name: bugreport
      description: write bugreport go given path
    - name: connect
      description: connect to a device via TCP/IP
    - name: devices
      description: list connected devices
      flags:
        -l: long output
    - name: disable-verity
      description: disable dm-verity checking on userdebug builds
    - name: disconnect
      description: disconnect from given TCP/IP device or all
    - name: emu
      description: run emulator console command
    - name: enable-verity
      description: re-enable dm-verity checking on userdebug builds
    - name: forward
      description: forward socket connection
      flags:
        --list: list all forward socket connections
        --no-rebind: don't replace existing connection
        --remove: remove specific forward socket connections
        --remove-all: remove all forward socket connections
    - name: get-devpath
      description: print <device-path>
    - name: get-serialno
      description: print <serial-number>
    - name: get-state
      description: print offline | bootloader | device
```

But most specs I get from that command doesn't use the full potential of carapace.

I will show some of the most useful ones:

https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-spec/carapace-spec/command/completion/flag.html
https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-spec/carapace-spec/macros/core.html
```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://carapace.sh/schemas/command.json
name: command
commands:
  - name: completion
    commands:
      - name: flag
        flags:
          -e?: executables
          -f, --file=: file
        completion:
          flag:
            e: ["$executables"]
            file: ["$files"]
```

https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-spec/carapace-spec/command/flags.html
```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://carapace.sh/schemas/command.json
name: command
commands:
  - name: flags
    flags:
      -b: bool flag
      -v=: shorthand with value
      --repeatable*: longhand repeatable
      -o, --optarg?: shorthand and longhand with optional argument
      --hidden&: longhand hidden
      --required!: longhand required
```


https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-spec/carapace-spec/command/completion/positional.html
```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://carapace.sh/schemas/command.json
name: command
commands:
  - name: completion
    commands:
      - name: positional
        completion:
          positional:
            - [pos1, positional1]
            - [pos2, positional2]
```


https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-spec/carapace-spec/command/completion/positionalAny.html
```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://carapace.sh/schemas/command.json
name: command
commands:
  - name: completion
    commands:
      - name: positionalany
        completion:
          positionalany: [posany, positionalany]
```


https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-spec/carapace-spec/command/exclusiveFlags.html
```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://carapace.sh/schemas/command.json
name: command
commands:
  - name: exclusiveflags
    flags:
      --add: add package
      --delete: delete package
    exclusiveflags:
      - [add, delete]
```


https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-spec/carapace-spec/command/persistentFlags.html
```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://carapace.sh/schemas/command.json
name: command
commands:
  - name: persistentflags
    persistentflags:
      -p, --persistent: persistent flag
    commands:
      - name: subcommand
        flags:
          -l, --local: local flag
```

https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-spec/carapace-spec/command/hidden.html
```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://carapace.sh/schemas/command.json
name: command
commands:
  - name: hidden
    hidden: true
    completion:
      positional:
        - [p1, positional1]
```


https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-bin/spec.html
```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://carapace.sh/schemas/command.json
name: mycmd
description: my command
flags:
  --optarg?: optarg flag
  -r, --repeatable*: repeatable flag
  -v=: flag with value
persistentflags:
  --help: bool flag
completion:
  flag:
    optarg: ["one", "two\twith description", "three\twith style\tblue"]
    v: ["$files"]
commands:
- name: sub
  description: subcommand
  completion:
    positional:
      - ["$list(,)", "1", "2", "3"]
      - ["$directories"]
```
The full available structure is:
https://carapace-sh.github.io/carapace-spec/carapace-spec/command.html
```go
type Command struct {
    Name            string
    Aliases         []string
    Description     string
    Group           string
    Hidden          bool
    Parsing         string
    Flags           map[string]string
    PersistentFlags map[string]string
    ExclusiveFlags  [][]string
    Run             string
    Completion      struct {
        Flag          map[string][]string
        Positional    [][]string
        PositionalAny []string
        Dash          [][]string
        DashAny       []string
    }
    Commands []Command
}
```


I'm currently almost finishing my work in a project, and I ended up just using argparse and an AI to write the script that outputs to carapace spec. After I finish that project I may save some time to work on implementing Carapace support for Click, though I’m unsure whether I’ll have the bandwidth, so if someone else wants to tackle it, please go ahead.
